title: D2C Payment, COD and Returns Reconciliation
summary: Reconcile your own website's orders with payment gateway settlements, courier COD remittances, RTO and refunds, so every order ends as paid, refunded, returned or chased.

seo.title: D2C Payment and COD Reconciliation | VipraTech
seo.description: Reconcile D2C website orders with payment gateway settlements, courier COD remittances, RTO and refunds, and chase every order that is still open.

designed_for: Founder or CFO of a D2C brand

problem.intro: D2C brands sell through their own website and collect money through payment gateways and cash on delivery. Gateways settle net of fees and refunds, couriers remit COD in batches after deducting their charges, and returned-to-origin orders reverse some of it. Matching orders to money received is a monthly spreadsheet exercise that misses COD that was collected but never remitted.

pain_points.title: COD collected but not remitted
pain_points.detail: Couriers remit COD in batches, and some delivered orders are never included.

pain_points.title: Gateway settlements net of everything
pain_points.detail: Settlements deduct fees, refunds and chargebacks, so they never equal the order total.

pain_points.title: RTO and refunds out of sync
pain_points.detail: Returned orders, cancellations and refunds are recorded in different systems and do not match the order status.

pain_points.title: Courier charges above contract
pain_points.detail: Freight and COD charges are deducted at rates or weights above the contract.

solution.overview: VipraTech takes orders from your store, settlements from your payment gateways, and remittances and invoices from your couriers, and gives every order a final status: paid, refunded, returned or still open. COD orders marked delivered are checked against courier remittances, and delivered orders with no remittance are listed for chasing. Gateway settlements are tied to orders net of fees and refunds, and courier charges are recalculated from the contract rates.
capabilities: Ties every order to its payment, refund or return
Finds delivered COD orders with no remittance
Reconciles gateway settlements net of fees, refunds and chargebacks
Recalculates courier freight and COD charges from contracts
Matches RTO and refunds to order status
List of open amounts by courier and gateway to chase

workflow.title: Collect
workflow.detail: Orders from the store, gateway settlements and courier remittances and invoices are gathered.

workflow.title: Tie payments
workflow.detail: Prepaid orders are matched to gateway settlements net of fees and refunds.

workflow.title: Tie COD
workflow.detail: Delivered COD orders are matched to courier remittances.

workflow.title: Check charges
workflow.detail: Courier freight and COD charges are recalculated from the contract.

workflow.title: Review
workflow.detail: Finance reviews open orders and overcharges.

workflow.title: Chase and close
workflow.detail: Open amounts are raised with couriers and gateways and tracked to closure.

inputs: Orders from Shopify, WooCommerce or your store
outputs: Delivered COD orders with no remittance
human_in_the_loop: Finance reviews open orders and overcharges and decides what to raise with couriers and gateways. The system prepares the list and evidence; it does not contact them.
integrations: Shopify, WooCommerce or custom store exports
Payment gateways such as Razorpay, Cashfree or PayU
Courier and aggregator reports such as Shiprocket or Delhivery
guardrails: No order closed without a matched payment, refund or return
Every overcharge shows the contract rate used
Open amounts aged by courier and gateway

pilot.scope: Two to three months of orders, one payment gateway and your main courier or aggregator.

what_we_measure.how: Share of orders with a final, matched status.
Value of delivered COD orders with no remittance, confirmed by finance.
Courier charge differences confirmed by finance.

faqs.q: We use an aggregator like Shiprocket. Does that work?
faqs.a: Yes. Aggregator reports carry the courier, COD and charges for each order, so they can be used directly.

faqs.q: Do you need our gateway or store login?
faqs.a: No. Report exports are enough to start.

faqs.q: Can it handle partial refunds and exchanges?
faqs.a: Yes. Each order keeps all its payments, refunds and exchanges, and its final balance is what is reconciled.
Distributor claims settlement is live today. D2C payment and COD reconciliation is in early access: we are building it with a small number of brands as design partners.
